Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopGlobal Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopGlobal's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jamie Chen, CEO; Taylor Brooks, CFO; Jordan Patel, COO; Riley Thompson, CMO; and Casey Nguyen, CTO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Chen, CEO of ShopGlobal.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q2 performance, driven by robust marketplace growth and expanding private label penetration. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV, which rose 18% year-over-year, alongside a 15% increase in active buyers.

Our focus remains on scaling our Global Fulfillment Network and enhancing customer retention through subscription perks. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our new AI-powered personalization engine, which we believe will significantly boost average order values and repeat purchase rates.

We are investing heavily in automation across our warehouses to drive fulfillment efficiencies.

We are focused on improving product mix toward higher-margin categories.

Finally, we are committed to navigating macroeconomic headwinds while delivering profitable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Brooks, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jamie. Our Q2 revenue was $4.2 billion, an increase of 15% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.5%, driven by product mix shifts, freight efficiencies, and supply chain optimizations. Operating expenses were $1.6 billion, representing 38% of revenue. Our marketing investments yielded strong returns, with customer acquisition costs stabilizing even as we ramped up app-focused campaigns.

Our net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $8.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance, which I'll detail shortly.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us on ShopGlobal's Q2 earnings call. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our gross margin performance, which remains a cornerstone of our profitability story in this competitive e-commerce landscape. For those unfamiliar, gross margin is calculated as net revenue minus cost of goods sold, or COGS, divided by net revenue. It encapsulates our pricing discipline, supply chain efficiency, and product mix optimization—key levers in online retail where scale can make or break margins.

Starting with the headline numbers: In Q2, we delivered a consolidated gross margin of 42.5%, up 230 basis points year-over-year from 40.2% in Q2 2023, and 80 basis points sequentially from Q1's 41.7%. This marks our 10th straight quarter of gross margin expansion, bringing our trailing four-quarter average to 41.8%—well above the industry peer average of around 38% for multi-category platforms like ours, and closing the gap with category leaders like Amazon, whose core retail margins hover in the low-40s.

To put this in perspective, back in Q4 2021, amid peak pandemic supply disruptions, our margins bottomed at 35.4%, hammered by freight inflation and inventory shortages. Since then, we've clawed back over 700 basis points through a multi-pronged strategy. Let me break down the key trends and drivers.

First, product mix shift remains the single largest tailwind. Our private label penetration reached 28% of GMV in Q2, up from 22% a year ago, driving an estimated 150 bps of expansion. Private labels—like our 'Global Essentials' line of consumer electronics and home goods—now average 52% gross margins, compared to 32% for third-party marketplace sellers. This mirrors success stories at peers like Walmart's bettergoods or Target's Good & Gather, but we're accelerating with AI-optimized assortment planning. Our new machine learning models analyze real-time search data and competitor pricing from platforms like Amazon and Temu, dynamically prioritizing high-margin SKUs in categories like small kitchen appliances (where we hit 48% margins) over lower-margin commoditized apparel (38%).

On the flip side, mix pressures persist in high-volume, low-margin verticals. Fashion and beauty, which grew 25% YoY to 15% of sales, capped out at 36% margins due to elevated return rates—our overall return rate ticked up to 18% from 16%, in line with industry norms amid 'bracketing' behavior where customers order multiple sizes. We're countering this with virtual try-on tech powered by AR, piloted in the US, which has already reduced fashion returns by 12% in test markets.

Second, COGS efficiencies, particularly in freight and fulfillment. Freight-in costs, a notorious margin-killer in e-commerce, fell 15% YoY as a percentage of sales, contributing 100 bps to expansion. Post-2022 rate normalization, ocean freight from Asia dropped to $2,500 per FEU from peaks of $10,000, and we've locked in multi-year contracts with carriers like Maersk at fixed rates. More strategically, our 'Global Fulfillment Network'—now spanning 45 owned warehouses and sortation centers across North America, Europe, and APAC—handled 65% of units in Q2, versus 50% last year. This has slashed last-mile delivery costs by 22%, with average fulfillment fees per unit down to $3.45 from $4.20.

We're investing heavily here: $250 million CapEx this year on robotics and automation, including goods-to-person systems from AutoStore akin to those at Ocado or Alibaba's Cainiao. Early ROI is promising—in our new Texas mega-hub, pick rates are up 40%, directly boosting throughput and margins by reducing labor-intensive handling.

Regionally, performance varied meaningfully. In North America, our largest market at 55% of revenue, margins expanded to 44.2% (+300 bps YoY), fueled by scale in Prime-like subscription perks driving repeat purchases and higher ASPs of $85 (up 8%). Europe, at 25% of sales, lagged at 39.8% (-50 bps YoY), pressured by VAT hikes in Germany and France, plus softer pricing power against Zalando and ASOS. That said, our UK private label ramp is gaining traction, with margins there improving 200 bps QoQ. APAC, now 18% of revenue post our Temu-competitive expansion into Southeast Asia, delivered 38.5% margins—solid for a high-growth region but challenged by lower ASPs ($45) and aggressive discounting to capture share from Shopee and Lazada. India specifically saw 15% YoY sales growth but 200 bps margin compression from hyper-local fulfillment investments.

Other factors worth noting: Promotional intensity rose modestly, with discounts averaging 22% of ASP (up from 20%), shaving 50 bps off margins but driving 18% GMV growth. We're mitigating via dynamic pricing algorithms that adjust in real-time based on elasticity data, similar to Amazon's demand forecasting. Inventory turns improved to 8.2x from 7.1x, reducing obsolescence costs by 30%, while supplier negotiations yielded 4-6% product cost reductions on electronics from partners in Vietnam and Mexico, hedging US-China tariffs.

Looking forward, we expect Q3 gross margins of 42.7-43.3%, with full-year guidance at 42.0-42.5%—implying another 200+ bps of YoY expansion. Risks include potential freight reflation if Red Sea disruptions persist, or mix dilution from grocery pilots (margins sub-25%). But our playbook is clear: double down on private labels to 35% penetration by 2025, expand owned logistics to 75% of volume, and leverage GenAI for predictive repricing to sustain pricing power.

In summary, our gross margin trajectory underscores ShopGlobal's transition from growth-at-all-costs to profitable scale, positioning us to outperform in an industry where peers like Wayfair and Etsy grapple with 30-35% margins amid macroeconomic headwinds.

Turning now to another key operational metric: fulfillment cost per order, or FCPO. In the e-commerce and online retail space, FCPO is a critical lever for profitability, capturing the end-to-end costs of picking, packing, shipping, last-mile delivery, and returns processing. It's directly tied to our ability to scale GMV while maintaining healthy unit economics, especially in a market where AOV hovers around $45 to $50 for many pure-play retailers like ours.

In Q2 2024, our FCPO came in at $7.12, marking a 12% sequential improvement from $8.09 in Q4 2023 and a robust 18% year-over-year decline from $8.67 in Q1 2023. This represents the lowest FCPO we've achieved since our pivot to hyper-local fulfillment in 2021, post the pandemic supply chain disruptions. For context, this is well below the industry benchmark of $9.50 to $11.00 reported by peers like Shopify merchants and Wayfair, and it's approaching Amazon's rumored sub-$7 FCPO in their core U.S. operations thanks to their scale.

This downward trajectory persists despite headwinds like a 5% rise in U.S. diesel prices and softening parcel rates from carriers like UPS and FedEx, which fell only 2-3% YoY after peaking in 2022. Our improvements are driven by a multi-pronged strategy focused on automation, network density, and data-driven optimization—putting us ahead of competitors like Overstock or Etsy, who have seen FCPO stagnation around $10 due to reliance on third-party logistics without proprietary tech stacks.

Key drivers include automation and robotics investments. We've deployed over 500 autonomous mobile robots—similar to Boston Dynamics' Stretch or Amazon's Hercules systems—in our top 15 fulfillment centers, which handle 65% of our North American volume. This has slashed pick-and-pack cycle times by 35%, from 45 seconds per item to under 30 seconds. In our new New Jersey mega-FC, co-located with ports for inbound efficiency, robotic arms integrated with goods-to-person systems have reduced labor content in fulfillment from 60% to 42% of total FCPO. CapEx here was $150 million last year, but it's already yielding a 3x ROI through 2025, with labor savings alone contributing $0.45 per order.

AI-powered route optimization and dynamic carrier allocation via our proprietary ZetaFlow AI engine, built on machine learning models trained on 2 billion+ historical shipments, now predicts delivery windows with 92% accuracy. This has cut last-mile costs by 22%, optimizing for real-time traffic, EV charging infrastructure, and carrier surcharges. We've shifted 40% of urban deliveries to electric vehicle fleets via partnerships with Rivian and our own ZetaFleet of 3,000 EVs, dodging fuel surcharges that hammered peers.

Returns optimization, using AI-driven Reverse Logistics Engine with computer vision to inspect 80% of returns at the FC level, automating resale grading. This has dropped returns processing costs from $4.50 to $3.20 per returned order, reclaiming 10% more inventory for resale, contributing $0.28 per order in savings.

Regionally, U.S. operations—85% of volume—saw FCPO fall to $6.85, a 20% YoY drop, fueled by 250+ micro-fulfillment centers enabling same-day delivery for 70% of subscribers. In Europe, FCPO improved to €7.90 ($8.55 equivalent) despite VAT and labor regs, with Ocado-inspired tech reducing labor by 28%. APAC FCPO at ¥850 ($5.70) faced typhoon disruptions but improved inbound efficiency by 18%.

Strategically, these improvements underscore our Dense Network Advantage—FCPO drops 8-10% for every 20% volume increase. We guide Q3 FCPO to $6.95-$7.10, full-year sub-$7.00, supported by $200 million CapEx.

Before moving on, let's address the impact of macroeconomic factors on our GMV and revenue. While we delivered resilient Q2 results with GMV of $15.2 billion, up 12% YoY but flat sequentially, and revenue of $4.2 billion, up 15% on take rate expansion, macro pressures have influenced our top line. Consumer wallets are tighter amid persistent inflation, elevated interest rates, and softening sentiment.

Inflation at 3.2% YoY eroded purchasing power, leading to a 15% YoY decline in non-essentials like apparel and electronics (45% of GMV), with luxury beauty down 22%. Essentials grew 18% to $4.8 billion GMV via QuickMart. AOV compressed 8% to $85, muting GMV but milder on revenue due to fulfillment fees.

Interest rates at 5.25-5.50% spiked delinquencies to 3.1%, curbing big-ticket items—home & garden and electronics down 25%, BNPL penetration to 22%. Supply chain volatility from Red Sea inflated freight 40%, but dynamic pricing cushioned.

Regionally, North America (65% GMV, +9%) saw essentials rebound but discretionary pullback; Europe (+8%) hit by energy inflation; APAC (+25%) boosted by stimulus; LATAM (+18%) pressured by FX.

We've mitigated with AI demand forecasting improving turns 22% to 8.5x, personalization lifting repeats to 48%, advertising to $850M (+28%), and cost discipline.

Seasonality also played a role this quarter. While Q2 isn't peak holiday, we analyze trends to explain deviations. Historically, Q4 drives 38-42% of annual GMV, but Q2 saw a 15% YoY GMV increase, capturing back-to-school and summer demand. Traffic surged 22%, mobile 68%, AOV $48 steady.

Deviations from expectations stemmed from macro headwinds shifting to essentials (discretionary +12% vs. 18% target), supply delays hitting electronics $250M short, and promotions eroding margins 150bps but boosting Cyber previews. Positive: AI pricing lifted GMV per seller 11%, recommendations up add-to-cart 25%.

Regionally, NA strong, Europe lagged, APAC outperformed. To smooth, we're expanding omnichannel BOPIS, NovaPrime to 45M (22% growth), JIT forecasting.

On mobile app engagement, a cornerstone of growth: Q2 new downloads 2.8 million, up 32% YoY, total 145M lifetime. MAU 18.2M (+22% YoY), DAU 5.6M (31% ratio), D7 retention 42%. App drove 42% GMV, conversion 5.1% (+28% YoY), AOV $68.

Technical: Flutter redesign cut loads 40%, ML personalization +32% CTR, push notifications 14% open. Targeting 30% GMV app share by 2025.

Now, turning to forward guidance for Q3 and full-year FY2024, and FY2025 outlook. As we navigate a maturing e-commerce landscape where penetration stabilizes at 20-22%, we remain confident through disciplined growth and tech investments.

Q3: Revenue $15.8-16.4B (+12-16% YoY), GMV $26.5-28.0B (+14-19%), Adj EBITDA $1.75-1.95B (11.0-11.9% margin).

Full FY2024: Revenue $59B implied.

FY2025: Revenue $66.0-69.0B (+12-16%), GMV $112-118B (+15-20%), Adj EBITDA $7.8-8.5B (11.8-12.3%), FCF $6-7B, EPS $4.85-5.35.

Drivers: US $36-38B (+13%), Europe $16-17B (+15%), APAC $10-11B (+18%), Emerging $3-3.5B (+25%). Marketplace 150K merchants, Elite subs 45M.

Assumes macro stability, hedged via AI. Investing $500M GenAI, blockchain. Risks: FX, competition, regs.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan to discuss operations.

Jordan Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. Operationally, we focused on expanding our fulfillment network and optimizing inventory management. Our shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs were down 18% year-over-year per order. We are implementing advanced robotics in 20 additional centers.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley.

Riley Thompson:
Thanks, Jordan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from our app-exclusive campaigns and personalized email series. Customer acquisition costs were $2.45. Our brand awareness increased by 20%. We are focusing on loyalty program enhancements and influencer partnerships.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey.

Casey Nguyen:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization and cloud infrastructure upgrades. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 22%. We're investing in GenAI for recommendation engines and blockchain for supply chain transparency.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question and answer session. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Sarah Lee with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Lee:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Taylor, can you expand on the gross margin drivers, especially private labels and regional variances? How sustainable is the expansion?

Taylor Brooks:
Thanks, Sarah. As I detailed, private labels at 28% of GMV drove 150 bps, with 52% margins vs. 32% third-party. Regional: NA 44.2%, Europe 39.8% challenged by VAT, APAC 38.5%. Sustainable via automation and AI repricing—guiding continued expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Rivera:
Great, thanks. On forward guidance, how does FY2025 revenue growth of 12-16% bake in macro assumptions, and what upside from new verticals?

Taylor Brooks:
Mike, guidance assumes 2-3% US spending growth, Fed cuts. Upside from groceries, health via acquisitions, APAC Singles Day. Tech like GenAI lifts AOV 7%, positioning for outperformance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan.

Emily Chen:
Thanks. Jordan, fulfillment costs improved sharply—can you talk trends and any new initiatives for Q3?

Jordan Patel:
Absolutely, Emily. FCPO at $7.12 reflects robotics slashing cycle times 35%, AI routes cutting last-mile 22%, returns optimization. Q3 adds 100 MFCs, targeting sub-$7 full-year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays.

David Kim:
Thanks. Riley, mobile app conversion hit 5.1%—impressive. How are you driving engagement amid rising CPI?

Riley Thompson:
David, downloads up 32% YoY via targeted UA, MAU 18.2M with 42% D7 retention from personalization. CPI $2.45 but 4.8x ROAS. Q4 live shopping to push 6%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Citi.

Lisa Wong:
Hi, thanks. Casey, macro impacted discretionary—how is tech stack mitigating, like on seasonality deviations?

Casey Nguyen:
Lisa, AI forecasting improved turns 22%, recommendations up repeats 48%. Seasonality smoothed via JIT, BOPIS 25% Q4 orders, NovaPrime insulating Q1 dips.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jamie Chen for closing remarks.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
